test_title: PYST 18: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - English Language (Held On 30 Jul, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Choose the correct meaning of the idiom:
'Rest on one's laurels'

options.text: To relax after failure and ignore work
To stop putting in effort after past success
To be jealous of others' achievements

solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2 i.e. To stop putting in effort after past success**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Rest on one's laurels"** means to stop trying to achieve something new because of satisfaction with past achievements. (अपने पिछले कामयाबियों से संतुष्ट होकर नई कोशिशें न करना)
 
 
• **Example:** After winning the award, she decided not to rest on her laurels but to continue working hard to achieve more success.
 
 
• In this context, it indicates that someone has achieved success in the past and is now not putting in further effort.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2 i.e. To stop putting in effort after past success**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: To relax after failure and ignore work** (असफलता के बाद आराम करना और काम को नज़रअंदाज करना)
 
 
• **Example:** This option refers to giving up after failure, which is not the meaning of the idiom.
 
 
 
 
• **Option 3: To dream about future victories** (भविष्य की जीत के बारे में सपने देखना)
 
 
• **Example:** This option refers to imagining future success, which is unrelated to the idiom's meaning.
 
 
 
 
• **Option 4: To be jealous of others' achievements** (दूसरों की उपलब्धियों से ईर्ष्या करना)
 
 
• **Example:** This option refers to envy, which is not the meaning of the idiom "Rest on one's laurels."
 
 

34:Tee6,
The correct answer is **Option 3**.
